clue.text: In middle distance, I entered university environment

indicators.note: I goes into the distance word, so 'entered' marks one piece placed inside another

parts.note: the mile is a classic middle-distance race, so the phrase gives MILE

explanation.surface: A runner muses on campus life somewhere in the middle of a race.
explanation.walkthrough: 'entered' puts I inside MILE, after its L, giving MILIE; U follows. 'In' at the start is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A milieu is the social setting or surroundings someone lives in.

clue.text: Dispute having a test about nothing

indicators.note: the test word goes round the zero, so 'about' signals a container

parts.note: the MOT is the annual British roadworthiness test for vehicles
O, the zero, stands for nothing

explanation.surface: An argument over an exam that came to nothing.
explanation.walkthrough: The MOT is Britain's yearly safety check on cars over three years old; 'about' wraps it round O.
explanation.definitionFit: To moot a point is to raise it for debate or argue it.

clue.text: Butter up some wild (initially tame) animal

indicators.note: in a down clue, 'up' means the word is written from the bottom upwards

parts.note: a ram butts with its head, so it is a butter

indicators.note: wild suggests disorder, so the letters are scrambled
initially points at the opening letter of the word tame

explanation.surface: Flatter a beast that is part wild and only tame at first.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Butter up' looks like flattery, but 'butter' is one that butts, a RAM, and 'up' turns it to MAR. 'wild' scrambles SOME plus T (the start of 'tame', marked by 'initially') into MOSET.
explanation.definitionFit: The marmoset is a small South American monkey.

clue.text: They try to breed chess champions

definitions.meaning: animals pairing off for breeding are those that mate
players who deliver checkmate are those that mate in chess

explanation.walkthrough: Both halves rest on 'mate': pairing to breed, and winning at chess.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses come from mating: breeders pair up, and chess winners checkmate their opponents.

clue.text: Work in a plant erected in China

indicators.note: the reversed plant sits inside the friend word, so this 'in' signals a container

parts.note: in cockney rhyming slang 'china plate' is mate, so China means mate

indicators.note: in a down clue something erected is stood upright, so it reads from the bottom up

parts.note: the lupin is a garden plant

explanation.surface: Labouring in a Chinese factory that has just been put up.
explanation.walkthrough: China is a pal in rhyming slang (china plate = mate). 'erected' turns A LUPIN into NIPULA, which goes inside MATE. The first 'in' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To manipulate something is to work it with the hands or handle it skilfully.

clue.text: Prate as a result of this Wednesday's sol instruction for STRAPPED hardware

annotationWithheld.why: Clue as held, 'Prate as a result of this Wednesday's sol instruction for STRAPPED hardware', is garbled by OCR with stray text; only 'Prate as a result of this ... hardware' reads as a clue
annotationWithheld.clue: Prate as a result of this Wednesday's sol instruction for STRAPPED hardware

clue.text: Power base wants volunteers back in outfit

indicators.note: the base word and reversed volunteers go inside the outfit, so 'in' marks a container

parts.note: a kit is a set of clothes or equipment, an outfit
base means low, as in base motives

indicators.note: back means the volunteers' letters are read in reverse

parts.note: TA, the Territorial Army, is Britain's volunteer reserve force

explanation.surface: A low-level operative wants recruits back in uniform.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns TA into AT; LOW and AT then go inside KIT. 'wants' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A kilowatt is a unit of power equal to a thousand watts.

clue.text: Unofficially handle weight above a setter

indicators.note: in a down clue, above means the weight comes before the rest

parts.note: a ton is a unit of weight
the crossword setter refers to himself as me

explanation.surface: A heavy crossword compiler gets a nickname.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'above' puts TON first; the setter of a puzzle is ME.
explanation.definitionFit: A to-name, chiefly Scots, is a nickname added to distinguish people with the same name, and 'handle' is slang for a name.

clue.text: Slow ace one serves in trouble

indicators.note: the ace and soldier go inside the trouble word, so 'in' marks a container

parts.note: ado means fuss or trouble
A is the ace in a pack of cards
a GI is an American soldier, one who serves

explanation.surface: A tennis player's ace serve is slow, and trouble follows.
explanation.walkthrough: 'serves' suggests tennis after 'ace', but 'one serves' is a GI, an American serviceman.
explanation.definitionFit: Adagio is the musical direction for a slow tempo.

clue.text: Garment 7 cut out slightly off-centre

indicators.note: a block of letters just past the middle of that entry is removed

parts.note: the reference is to the answer at 7 across, the power unit

explanation.surface: A garment cut a little off-centre by a tailor.
explanation.walkthrough: The middle four letters of 7 across would be LOWA; the four cut out, OWAT, sit one place to the right, hence 'slightly off-centre'.
explanation.definitionFit: A kilt is the pleated knee-length skirt of Highland dress.

clue.text: One vomited — terrible — or capital!

indicators.note: something terrible is in a bad state, so these letters are shaken up

explanation.surface: Someone was violently sick, which is either awful or marvellous.
explanation.walkthrough: 'capital' as an exclamation means 'excellent', but it is the definition: a capital city.
explanation.definitionFit: Montevideo is the capital city of Uruguay.

clue.text: Muskrats endlessly soiled shirts in 25?

indicators.note: soiled means made a mess of, so the letters are jumbled
endlessly means the first and last letters of the word are dropped

explanation.surface: Muskrats have left shirts dirty in some far-off place.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endlessly' strips Muskrats to USKRAT; 'soiled' scrambles those letters. 25 across is KERALA, an Indian state, hence the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: Kurtas are long loose collarless shirts worn in South Asia, including the state at 25.

clue.text: Canine itch sorted by expert

indicators.note: sorted means put in order, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A dog's itch is dealt with by a specialist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sorted' reads as 'cured', but it signals an anagram of CANINE ITCH.
explanation.definitionFit: A technician is a skilled specialist in a craft or technical field.

clue.text: Little man breaking low buzzer

indicators.note: the small person breaks into the cow's call, so 'breaking' signals insertion

parts.note: to low is to moo like cattle
a squit is British slang for a small or insignificant person

explanation.surface: A small fellow interrupts a low buzzing sound.
explanation.walkthrough: 'low' is the cow's call, MOO, not 'not high'; 'breaking' puts SQUIT (British slang for a little nobody) inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: The insect is called a buzzer for the whine of its wings.

clue.text: Former convict's leader that's accepting time in stir

parts.note: ex means former

indicators.note: leader points at the first letter of convict
the abbreviation takes in the time letter, so 'accepting' marks a container

parts.note: i.e. is the abbreviation for 'that is'

explanation.surface: An ex-con's ringleader is doing time in prison.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stir' is slang for prison, which fits the surface, but here it is the verb 'rouse'. 'accepting' puts T inside IE.
explanation.definitionFit: To excite feelings is to stir them up.

clue.text: New general bombed part of Germany

indicators.note: bombed means blown apart, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A newly appointed commander bombed a German region.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bombed' scrambles N and GENERAL together.
explanation.definitionFit: Erlangen is a university city in Bavaria, southern Germany.

clue.text: Came upon evenly prepared pitch?

indicators.note: prepared means made ready, so the letters are reworked
evenly picks the second and fourth letters of upon

explanation.surface: Someone stumbled on a well-groomed playing field.
explanation.walkthrough: 'evenly' takes the even letters of 'upon', P and N, and 'prepared' scrambles them with CAME. 'pitch' is a tent, not a sports field.
explanation.definitionFit: To pitch tents is to set up camp, hence the question mark.

clue.text: A 17 A number of people accepting, say, denial

indicators.note: the people word takes in the example abbreviation, so 'accepting' marks a container

parts.note: a nation is a large body of people
e.g. means 'for example', which is what 'say' means here

explanation.surface: A crowd that takes something on board, then refuses it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'say' gives EG, for example, which 'accepting' puts inside NATION.
explanation.definitionFit: Negation is the act of denying or contradicting something.

clue.text: Expel shoplifter, ultimately entering store

indicators.note: the last letter goes into the storehouse word, so 'entering' signals insertion

parts.note: a depot is a storehouse

indicators.note: ultimately points at the final letter of shoplifter

explanation.surface: A thief caught walking into a shop is thrown out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ultimately' gives R, which 'entering' puts inside DEPOT.
explanation.definitionFit: To deport someone is to expel them from a country.

clue.text: Broadcasts linked OK in a rush

indicators.note: broadcasting scatters things widely, so these letters are spread and rearranged

explanation.surface: A news report said everything was linked and fine during a busy period.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Broadcasts' looks like the subject, but it scatters LINKED OK; 'in' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The Klondike in Canada's Yukon was the scene of the gold rush of 1896-99.

clue.text: Man touring poor African city

indicators.note: the name goes round the poor word, so 'touring' marks a container

parts.note: Ian is a man's name
poor means bad, as in poor work

explanation.surface: A fellow visits a deprived city in Africa.
explanation.walkthrough: 'touring' wraps IAN round BAD.
explanation.definitionFit: Ibadan is a large city in south-western Nigeria.

clue.text: Man races in run for a quarter?

indicators.note: the man and races go inside the run word, so 'in' marks a container

parts.note: go means run, as a machine goes
he, the pronoun, stands for a man
the TT races are motorcycle races on the Isle of Man

explanation.surface: A man running in the Isle of Man races takes a quarter-mile leg.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Man races' points at the Isle of Man TT, but HE and TT are separate pieces, both put inside GO by 'in'. The quarter is a district.
explanation.definitionFit: A ghetto is a quarter of a city where one group lives, hence the question mark.

clue.text: A heartless poet's verse

indicators.note: heartless means the middle letters of the poet's name are removed

parts.note: Alfred Tennyson was the Victorian Poet Laureate

explanation.surface: A cold, uncaring poet's lines.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heartless' removes NY, the two central letters of TENNYSON.
explanation.definitionFit: A tenson is a Provencal troubadour verse contest, two poets disputing in alternate stanzas.

clue.text: A baker's beginning to cut excellent loaf

indicators.note: the pieces cut into the excellent word, so this marks insertion

parts.note: a knockout is something outstandingly good

indicators.note: beginning points at the first letter of baker

explanation.surface: A baker starts slicing a superb loaf of bread.
explanation.walkthrough: 'loaf' is the bread a baker makes, but here it is the verb: to idle about. 'to cut' puts A and B inside KNOCKOUT.
explanation.definitionFit: To knock about is to loaf around aimlessly.

clue.text: Flatten Geordie back inside bingo

indicators.note: the reversed letters sit within the knockout, so 'inside' marks a container

parts.note: KO, a knockout, flattens an opponent

indicators.note: back means the letters are read in reverse

parts.note: a Geordie comes from Newcastle in the North East of England, NE

explanation.surface: Knocking down a Newcastle man playing bingo.
explanation.walkthrough: A Geordie is from Newcastle, in England's North East: NE, which 'back' turns to EN inside KO.
explanation.definitionFit: Keno is a lottery game played with numbered cards, much like bingo.

clue.text: Fire left smothered by family

indicators.note: the left letter is covered on both sides by the family word, so this marks a container

parts.note: kin are your family

explanation.surface: A fire on the left put out by relatives.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fire' looks like a noun, but it is a verb: to bake in a kiln. 'smothered by' puts L inside KIN.
explanation.definitionFit: To kiln pottery or bricks is to bake them in an oven, which is firing them.

clue.text: Some agents-general are kept back in a state

indicators.note: back means that part is read in reverse
some means only part of the words is taken

explanation.surface: Some diplomats are held back in a foreign country.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Some' takes ALAREK from 'agents-generAL ARE Kept', and 'back' reverses it. 'in' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Kerala is a state on the south-west coast of India.

clue.text: In addition, sign into party — cheers

parts.note: too means in addition, also

indicators.note: the star sign goes into the party word, so 'into' signals insertion

parts.note: a do is a party
Leo is a sign of the zodiac

explanation.surface: Someone signs in at a party and says cheers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cheers' reads as a toast, but in British use it also means goodbye. 'into' puts LEO inside DO.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are informal British farewells, ways of saying goodbye.
